newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes soar on weather, seen overdone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes soar on weather, seen overdone.

text.p: U.S. Crude oil prices soared Monday as futures prices tracked heating oil higher on forecasts for freezing weather across much of the country.
But some traders said they see gains as overdone and expect a sharp retracement over the next couple of days.

"I don't think it has any business being up this high, especially with figures coming out tomorrow," said one trader, referring to the American Petroleum Institute weekly report due out after futures markets close on Tuesday.
Benchmark West Texas Intermediate at Cushing was up more than $1.20 at around $25.70 a barrel in early afternoon.

Last week's API report showed an extraordinarily high level of gasoline production and another sharp rise in heating oil inventories. Some traders said they expect another heating oil build in inventories in Tuesday's report.
"You've got to remember the bearish factors that only last week gave us the biggest two-day drop in a long, long while," said a senior Houston-based trader at a major oil company.

The milder-than-normal weather in the eastern U.S. in the first half of December, cheaper North Sea crude and the long-delayed resumption of Iraqi oil exports under the United Nations humanitarian deal have not disappeared because of a forecast cold snap, he points out.

Meanwhile, the sweet/sour differential closed up around 10 cents in early trading Monday. Extra supply from the U.S. government and Latin American had pushed the WTI/WTS differential out all year, reaching $1.75 or so in the past two months compared with more typical levels of around $1.00.
WTS traded early at $1.64 below benchmark WTI/Cushing.

Other actively-traded domestic grades were steady to a touch firmer, with posted plus up about 10 cents on differential at $2.36 above. WTI/Midland traded at evens, while Light Louisiana traded at a 68-cent premium, within last Friday's ranges.

Meanwhile, soaring WTI blew its premium against Brent out to $1.55 on January from around $1.20 late last week. But like the rest of the market, traders were skeptical that this level would be sustained.
